pl-l4d26c1-d1e115.summary: States that while other sacraments began after and because of sin, the sacrament of marriage is read to have been instituted by the Lord before sin, not as a remedy but as a duty.
claims: Marriage was instituted before sin, as a duty.

pl-l4d26c1-d1e121.summary: Recounts Genesis: when sleep was sent on Adam and a rib taken to form the woman, Adam, understanding in spirit for what purpose she was made, said prophetically after his ecstasy: this now is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; so a man shall leave father and mother and cleave to his wife, and they shall be two in one flesh.

pl-l4d26c1.summary: Introduces marriage: unlike other sacraments, instituted after and because of sin, marriage was instituted by the Lord before sin, not as remedy but as duty. Genesis recounts that Adam, after the woman was formed from his rib, prophetically said 'this now is bone of my bones; therefore a man shall leave father and mother and cleave to his wife, and they shall be two in one flesh'.
claims: Marriage was instituted before sin as a duty.
Other sacraments were instituted after sin.
